question: Under identical training, does frozen measured VNC outperform amplitude-matched random and degree-preserving rewired cores through a 4-command trainable body interface?
pilot_clause: 5M environment steps per arm is a compute-limited pilot; if no arm reaches stable forward locomotion, label EMBODY-PILOT-INCONCLUSIVE and make no connectivity conclusion.

interface_architecture.class: Linear encoder → frozen VNC rate core → Linear motor decoder
interface_architecture.encoder_output: 4 fixed latent commands expanded by anatomy-derived command map
interface_architecture.decoder_input: all 260 VNC motor-output channels; common-mask sensitivity reported separately
interface_architecture.recurrent_state: one frozen VNC rate per node

stage1.method: supervised interface fit to an Option-B body-path teacher; core frozen

stage2.method: batched on-policy PPO with the measured vector-environment throughput choice
stage2.selection: last fixed checkpoint; no evaluation-distance selection

endpoints.primary: mean forward displacement (m) per held-out-seed evaluation episode at fixed final checkpoint

pre_registered_null: connectome ties or loses to the amplitude-matched random arm under identical training → the structural advantage does not survive a trainable interface; the moat is zero-training-only.

motor_channel_sensitivity.primary: all 260 motor channels; excluded channels remain in decoder with declared identity affine
motor_channel_sensitivity.common_mask_sensitivity: 52 channels varying in all three calibration histories; report separately without retuning

static_input_diagnostic.reason: optional arm deferred; CPU-only host and three required arms take precedence
